title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 sketchbook geolocation audit
scope: Backend-only spatial calibration of selected filmed sketchbook pages against correspondence, historical maps, landmark geometry and landscape form.
frontend_policy: Do not expose this image-derived layer or any sketchbook image on public Pages in this phase.

method.principle: Represent the precision actually supported by the evidence. Do not convert field areas, travel corridors or inferred sightlines into false exact points.
method.modern_coordinate_guard: Modern coordinates are used only as geometric control points. They do not by themselves prove a nineteenth-century viewpoint.

baseline.label: Maricopa railroad settlement/station vicinity
baseline.coordinate_status: approximate modeling baseline, not a surveyed 1892 viewpoint

terrain_candidates.name: Sierra Estrella / Hayes Peak sector
terrain_candidates.reason: Long rugged range rising beyond a broad desert plain is compatible with the sketch; Sierra Estrella is a major continuous range northwest of Maricopa.

terrain_candidates.name: Table Top Mountains sector
terrain_candidates.reason: Comparable distance but a different viewing direction; retained until horizon profiles or a more diagnostic peak form resolves orientation.

current_result.recommended_geometry: field-area ellipse/polygon around Maricopa desert, with candidate sightline NW to Sierra Estrella stored only as hypothesis

cases.assessment: Same-day Maricopa landscape group. Mountain identification remains open; Sierra Estrella is currently the leading range candidate, not a secure identification.
cases.recommended_geometry: same Maricopa field-area object as p04-p05, but preserve page-level distinction

reasoning: The sketch follows the securely dated Maricopa group in the filmed sequence and precedes the Hesperia group.

Rudolf's San Diego retrospective account explicitly describes a rocky range behind chaparral and cactus across Arizona to Yuma, then a widening near-barren California desert, the below-sea-level Salton depression, and finally a climb past snow-covered San Jacinto.
The sketch shows a large steep rocky massif rising abruptly from sparse stony desert, compatible with a San Jacinto/Colorado Desert view but not diagnostic enough for a point.

terrain_model.assessment: Both high-peak controls lie southeast from Hesperia. This agrees with a general southeast viewing sector for the mountain backdrop, but the modeled baseline is too coarse to identify a specific summit from the drawing.

current_result.recommended_geometry: field-area around the 1891 townsite/depot plus a broad SE view sector; route-revision candidate 5 May

view_model.hypothesis: shipboard point offshore north of Port Antonio, looking generally south into/along the harbour entrance
view_model.example_point_status: illustrative geometry only, not a claimed historical position
view_model.sensitivity: Moving the modeled ship position farther north decreases Folly-Navy angular separation: about 44 degrees at latitude 18.200, 32 degrees at 18.205, 25 degrees at 18.210, and 20 degrees at 18.215 along longitude -76.448.
view_model.assessment: The left/right landmark order is robust for an offshore northern approach. Distance offshore remains unresolved because the artist's field of view and scale are unknown.

current_result.recommended_geometry: broad offshore approach corridor / view sector north of the harbour, never an exact point

cases.assessment: Both are laid-in tropical water/palm drawings and visually belong to the same material group as p23. Port Antonio is plausible after the p23 landmark match, but neither page has a diagnostic landmark yet.

current_result.recommended_geometry: unmapped candidate association until shoreline/building topology can be matched

research_conclusions: The filmed sketchbook begins, as presently observable, with Maricopa material dated 24 April rather than a securely visible Tempe 22 April page; preserve this as a catalogue-surrogate conflict.
The sketchbook supplies environmental and viewpoint evidence that is different from the taxon-centered botanical study drawings used in Corning 2007.
Maricopa, Hesperia and Port Antonio can already be represented at finer spatial scales than city markers, but only in the backend and with explicit geometry classes and confidence.
Page 23 is the strongest new geolocation candidate because a lighthouse-island configuration can be tested geometrically against Folly Point and Navy Island.
Page 17 is the strongest image-text fieldwork match because the Joshua-tree landscape and mountain backdrop closely track Rudolf's Hesperia description.
next_work: Obtain/download the full-resolution Huntington Hesperia maps and georeference the 1891 depot/townsite.
Generate terrain horizon profiles from plausible Maricopa station/desert viewpoints toward Sierra Estrella and Table Top, then compare peak order to pages 5 and 9.
Use the Port Antonio Admiralty chart plus current landmark coordinates to create a view-sector polygon for p23 and test p21/p25 against adjacent harbour orientations.
Test p12/p13 against San Jacinto silhouettes from the 1892 Southern Pacific/Yuma-Salton-Indio corridor before assigning any named mountain.
Keep all resulting image references and spatial hypotheses in research/backend only.
